To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the traditional approach to Phase I trials of anticancer drugs (i.e., dose escalation until the MTD is reached) should be replaced by a strategy that escalates systemic exposure (i.e., area under the concentration time curve [AUC]) until the MTSE is reached.
the concept of MTSE, defined as the AUC at the MTD, is an important concept that can be used to facilitate the design of Phase I trials of anticancer drugs.

the development of a new paradigm for Phase I-II studies of cancer chemotherapy.

this strategy is a novel, promising approach to Phase I trials, which should permit more rapid and more precise dose escalation and, most importantly, more precisely define the maximum level of systemic exposure for future Phase II studies.

a Phase I study should be designed in a manner that allows for the most rapid and accurate determination of the MTD, or MTSE, and the MTD or MTSE should be used as the starting point for a Phase II study.

a Phase I trial is a study that determines the MTD of an investigational anticancer drug in humans and is the initial step in a series of clinical trials that are designed to establish the effectiveness of the drug in humans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) of an anticancer drug should be defined as the dose that results in the maximum level of systemic exposure (MTS) that can be tolerated without excessive toxic effects.
the maximum tolerated dosage is a poor surrogate for maximum tolerated systemic exposure.
we are not yet able to predict the MTD in humans from preclinical data.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the maximum tolerated dosage in humans is not the same as the maximum tolerated systemic exposure, and the latter is more important for determining the optimal dosage to use in subsequent Phase II trials.
the concept of maximum tolerated systemic dose (MTSE) may be more relevant for the design and conduct of Phase I-II trials than the concept of maximum tolerable dosage (MTD).

the concept of maximum tolerated systemic drug exposure is a useful and practical tool for designing Phase I trials of anticancer drugs, and that the MTSE is a useful and important endpoint for Phase I studies.
